title: Extract a TextTransformer trait from Rust string-utils free functions
description: A Rust library exposes text utilities as free functions. Refactor them behind a TextTransformer trait implemented by a DefaultTransformer struct, enabling alternative implementations.

task_spec.prompt:
The library in src/lib.rs has two public free functions: word_count(s: &str) -> usize and capitalize_words(s: &str) -> String. Refactor as follows:

1. Define a trait TextTransformer with two methods: fn word_count(&self, s: &str) -> usize and fn capitalize_words(&self, s: &str) -> String.

2. Create a struct DefaultTransformer (unit struct or empty struct) that implements TextTransformer by delegating to the existing logic.

3. Keep the original free functions (word_count and capitalize_words) as public free functions for backwards compatibility — they can delegate to DefaultTransformer or contain the original logic.

4. Add a constructor pub fn new_transformer() -> impl TextTransformer that returns a DefaultTransformer.

5. Update or add tests: add test_transformer_word_count and test_transformer_capitalize that construct a DefaultTransformer and call its trait methods. All original tests must still pass.

Run cargo test to confirm all tests pass. Run cargo clippy -- -D warnings to confirm no warnings.
required_artifacts: TextTransformer trait with word_count and capitalize_words methods
Original free functions preserved for backwards compatibility
success_criteria: Trait enables mock implementations in downstream tests
Backwards-compatible: existing callers using free functions still compile
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test` to confirm no regressions from your refactor. Also review the code you changed — any remaining duplication, long functions, or unclear names to clean up?
Final pass: run `cargo test` and confirm everything is green. Give me a one-line summary of what changed.
